heading.en: Why are there gaps in railway tracks?

hook.en: Look closely at old railway lines: small gaps are left between rails. On a hot afternoon the steel grows longer, and without the gaps the track would buckle.
hook.kn: ಹಳೆಯ ರೈಲು ಹಳಿಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಂತರ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಬಿಸಿ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಉಕ್ಕು ಉದ್ದವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಅಂತರವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಹಳಿ ಬಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು.

objectives.en: Use the coefficients of linear, area and volume expansion
Explain the anomalous expansion of water

narration.en: Look closely at old railway lines: small gaps are left between rails. On a hot afternoon the steel grows longer, and without the gaps the track would buckle.
narration.kn: ಹಳೆಯ ರೈಲು ಹಳಿಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಂತರ ಬಿಟ್ಟಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಬಿಸಿ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಉಕ್ಕು ಉದ್ದವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಅಂತರವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಹಳಿ ಬಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು.

body.en: Most substances expand on heating. For a small rise ΔT, ΔL/L = α_l ΔT, ΔA/A = α_A ΔT and ΔV/V = α_V ΔT. For an isotropic solid α_A = 2α_l and α_V = 3α_l. Metals have α_l of the order of 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. If a rod is clamped so it cannot expand, a thermal stress YαΔT develops.
body.kn: ಬಿಸಿ ಮಾಡಿದಾಗ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ವ್ಯಾಕೋಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ: ΔL/L = α_l ΔT, ΔV/V = α_V ΔT. ಸಮದಿಶೀಯ ಘನಕ್ಕೆ α_A = 2α_l, α_V = 3α_l. ಹಿಡಿದಿಟ್ಟ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಉಷ್ಣ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ YαΔT ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Water contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C, so it is densest at 4 °C. In winter the top of a lake cools and sinks until the whole lake is at 4 °C; then the surface freezes first while water below stays at about 4 °C, and fish survive.
body.kn: ನೀರು 0 °C ನಿಂದ 4 °C ವರೆಗೆ ಬಿಸಿಮಾಡಿದಾಗ ಸಂಕುಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; 4 °C ನಲ್ಲಿ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸರೋವರದ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಮೊದಲು ಹೆಪ್ಪುಗಟ್ಟುತ್ತದೆ, ಕೆಳಗಿನ ನೀರಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೀನುಗಳು ಬದುಕುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Lakes freeze from the top down

narration.en: Water contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C, so it is densest at 4 °C. In winter the top of a lake cools and sinks until the whole lake is at 4 °C; then the surface freezes first while water below stays at about 4 °C, and fish survive.

problem.en: A steel rail is 10 m long at 20 °C. How much longer is it at 60 °C? (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A steel rail is 10 m long at 20 °C. How much longer is it at 60 °C? (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)

body.en: Linear, area and volume expansion coefficients of an isotropic solid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 — one for each dimension that grows.

narration.en: 1 : 2 : 3. Linear, area and volume expansion coefficients of an isotropic solid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 — one for each dimension that grows.

homework.en: A brass disc of radius 5 cm (α = 1.9 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹) is heated by 100 K. Find the increase in its area.
